title: Article 14 — Equality before law and equal protection of the laws

content.overview: Article 14 forbids the State from denying to any person equality before the law or the equal protection of the laws within the territory of India. Classification is permitted if it rests on an intelligible differentia bearing a rational nexus to the object of the law. Arbitrary State action is inconsistent with equality.

sections.heading: Two limbs
sections.body: Equality before the law and equal protection of the laws. The first is associated with the absence of special privilege; the second with equal application of the laws to persons similarly situated.

sections.heading: Reasonable classification
sections.body: Valid classification requires (1) an intelligible differentia distinguishing the group included from those left out, and (2) a rational relation between that differentia and the object of the statute. Class legislation without such basis fails.

sections.heading: Non-arbitrariness
sections.body: Modern Article 14 review also asks whether State action is arbitrary. Manifest arbitrariness has been used as a standard for invalidating certain measures — apply it from controlling authorities; do not invent holdings.

sections.heading: Track B
sections.body: Plead the class, the object, the differentia, the nexus failure or the arbitrariness in operation. Do not plead Article 14 as a slogan.
